History:
• 26-year-old female presents with a “crazy” headache that began ~3 days ago while at work and has progressively worsened.  
• Location: diffuse but maximal around the right eye.  
• Character: dull constant ache with intermittent sharper spikes; severity 8/10.  
• Course: present continuously; intensity fluctuates.  
• Associated symptoms: photophobia (“light hurts”), brief “shooting lights” at onset, nausea without vomiting, difficulty concentrating.  
• No documented fever, neck stiffness, focal weakness, speech difficulty, visual loss, trauma, or skin rash.  
• Triggers/relief: sleep and ibuprofen (three tablets daily, dose not specified) provided no relief; reduced computer-screen brightness helps slightly.  
• Similar episodes: prior mild headaches responsive to ibuprofen; first episode of this severity.  
• Family history: mother and sister with recurrent migraines.  
• Social/occupational: IT job with prolonged screen time; lives with three housemates; social smoker and drinker; mild work stress.  
• Ideas/concerns: worried this may be migraine; seeks stronger medication.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic illnesses: none reported.  
• Surgeries/hospitalizations: not recorded.  
• Medications: none regularly; ibuprofen self-administered (dose/route/frequency not fully documented).  
• Allergies: no known drug allergies.  
• Gynecologic: use of oral contraceptive pill not documented.

Physical Examination:
• General appearance (video): patient alert and conversant.  
• No focal neurologic deficits reported.  
• No other physical findings recorded (virtual visit).

Impression:
Likely migraine headache, first clinically significant episode.  
Alternate considerations (consistent with transcript):  
1. Tension-type headache – diffuse dull pain and work stress but photophobia/aura less typical.  
2. Acute sinusitis – right-periorbital pain, but absent sinus/nasal symptoms make this less likely.

Management Plan:
• Education: explained migraine as most probable cause given presentation and family history.  
• Analgesia options discussed:  
  – Optimize ibuprofen dosing (up to 400 mg × 2 tablets three times daily with food).  
  – Prescribe naproxen (dose/route/frequency to be provided on prescription).  
  – Consider adding paracetamol or codeine for additional pain control.  
• Headache diary: record timing, severity, potential triggers (sleep, hydration, screen time, stress).  
• Follow-up: scheduled in 1–2 weeks to assess response; earlier review advised if headaches increase, vision changes, limb weakness, or general deterioration.  
• Preventive therapy: discuss prophylactic migraine medication at follow-up if attacks recur.

Patient Summary:
26-year-old woman with a 3-day worsening right-predominant headache, photophobia, visual phenomena, and nausea—features most consistent with a first episode of migraine. Provided stronger analgesic plan and safety-net instructions; will reassess in 1–2 weeks.

Key Takeaways:
• Start prescribed naproxen (or optimized ibuprofen) and may combine with paracetamol/codeine as directed.  
• Keep a detailed headache diary to identify patterns or triggers.  
• Seek immediate care if vision changes, limb weakness, severe worsening, or other concerning symptoms occur.

Next Steps:
• Dispense prescription today.  
• Re-evaluation appointment in 1–2 weeks; sooner if no improvement.  
• If headaches become frequent, consider prophylactic migraine therapy and arrange eye examination to rule out visual strain.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing typical data: vital signs, full neurologic exam, neck examination, weight/BMI, menstrual/OCP history, detailed ibuprofen dose.  
• Conflicts: transient “Yeah” then “No” to neck stiffness question—unclear; treated as no stiffness.  
• Transcript quality: clear overall; minor false starts and overlapping speech but adequate clinical detail.
